answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Grove Rule. Each agent identity keeps a public commitment to its action history; at epoch boundaries the agent must produce a cipher proving the new epoch's first actions continue the prior epoch's committed behaviour chain, verified against the stored root. An identity that resets or diverges fails continuity and is excluded. To forge a convincing fresh identity, an attacker must re-run the entire prior behavioural history to regenerate a valid chain commitment, paying full compute and interaction cost per synthetic identity every epoch rather than a one-time fee.
